classification.theory_summary: Presents survey results (171 respondents) and argues Mallworld dreams correlate with trauma/psychedelic use and show high long-term navigable spatial consistency; proposes MKUltra/NLP-related cultural trauma programming hypothesis.
classification.skip_reason: No single dream narrative; post is survey results + theory discussion. Extractable content is aggregate/claimed common features rather than a specific dream experience.

meta.author_theory: Mallworld dreams are a shared-structure phenomenon correlated with trauma/psychedelic exposure; proposes link to widespread cultural trauma response and neuro-linguistic programming/MKUltra-adjacent experimentation; emphasizes persistent navigable structure across dreams.

extraction.extraction_notes: Post contains no first-person dream scene. Phenomenological content appears as aggregate claims from survey results: recurring/navigable geography over time; mixed settings (multiple location types); populated areas with non-interacting 'NPC-like' people; motivations in-dream (explore, achieve objectives, escape/run from pursuer); timeline/onset ages. Images are linked chart screenshots (survey graphs), not a hand-drawn map.
